speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Serum sickness-like reaction to amoxicillin.

The timeline of symptoms appearing one week after starting antibiotics, combined with the specific rash distribution (antecubital and popliteal fossae) and generalized joint pain, is classic for this diagnosis. Given the normal CBC and liver function tests, I do not need further imaging or blood work; the clinical picture is sufficient for this conclusion.
